This policy explains how CapitalCraft Studios ("we", "our", or "us") processes information when you use the Money Tycoon mobile application ("Money Tycoon" or the "App") on Android or iOS. Money Tycoon is a simulation game. Balances, holdings, trades, and other financial values inside the game are virtual game data, not real bank or brokerage accounts.

On both platforms this includes your player name, selected country and persona, virtual balances, businesses, properties, investments, orders, achievements, settings, tutorial state, and purchase entitlement state.
Anonymous account and optional linked identity

Google Play processes purchases. We receive purchase tokens, product identifiers, transaction status, and entitlement information needed to verify and deliver a purchase.
Apple App Store processes purchases through StoreKit. We receive transaction identifiers, product identifiers, and entitlement information needed to verify and deliver a purchase.
We do not receive full payment-card or bank-account details on either platform.

Firebase Cloud Messaging (Android) and Apple Push Notification service (iOS) may issue a per-installation token. When registered, the App may store the token with your Firebase user ID, locale, selected country, notification preferences, app version, device model, and OS version. In-app notification settings and OS permission controls determine whether notifications are shown. Server-side frequency controls limit engagement messages.

On Android, Google Play Games sign-in is optional. If used, the App may receive a Player ID and display name for authentication, achievements, Saved Games, and global leaderboards. The App may submit game statistics such as virtual net worth, business/property counts, passive income, prestige, achievements, trade profit, and virtual tax paid. These leaderboard scores are reported by the game client and are not verified from a server-owned gameplay ledger; the App labels that limitation on the leaderboard screen.
Google Play Games is not available on iOS. Empire leaderboards on iOS use on-device records and, when online features are enabled, Firestore-backed boards.

On both platforms, the App may show passive inline banner ads to free players on selected informational screens. It also offers rewarded ads and rewarded-interstitial bonus offers that play only after you deliberately choose to watch.

Google AdMob and enabled mediation partners may process an advertising or device identifier, your IP address and the approximate location derived from it, ad interactions, and diagnostic information about ad performance for ad delivery, measurement, frequency control, fraud prevention, and compliance. Depending on region and consent, ads may be personalized or non-personalized.

Firebase Analytics and Firebase Crashlytics may collect app interactions, crash logs, diagnostics, device information, and an anonymous user ID where privacy law requires consent (for example the EEA and UK), and may be enabled by default elsewhere. You can revisit consent choices from Settings.

Google Analytics for Firebase stays off until the app has received its remote configuration. In regions where privacy law requires consent (for example the EEA and UK), it is turned on only after you agree in the Google User Messaging Platform (UMP) consent form; elsewhere it is turned on by default. It is never turned on for players flagged as children (the child setting or an under-13 age answer). Advertising uses of your device's advertising identifier require your permission through Apple's App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompt, which you can change in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking; a "Do Not Sell My Data" choice keeps advertising uses off. Where privacy law requires consent, you can change your choice at any time in Settings → About → Manage Privacy Options. When on, it collects app-instance usage events (including

), in-app purchase events (product, price, currency), ad-impression revenue, and approximate location derived from your IP address. It also collects gameplay and app-usage events: the screens you open, the features you use and your progress in the game (for example career, business and finance milestones, daily claims and rewards, onboarding and tutorial steps and in-game choices), each recorded as a short fixed label, an item identifier from the game or a number, never text you typed; it also sets analytics properties such as a random test-group label used for game experiments. It also collects store and offer events: when you open the in-game store, which product you start to buy (the App Store product identifier), whether that purchase completes, is cancelled or fails (with a short failure reason such as "network error", never a message you typed), and whether you accept or dismiss the first-purchase offer. All of these events are keyed to a random app-instance ID, not to your account. If you installed the game after tapping an Apple Search Ads ad, the app also asks Apple, once per install, which ad led to the install (Apple's AdServices framework; this does not use the advertising identifier and needs no tracking permission). We keep whether the install came from an ad, the campaign, ad group and keyword identifiers, the Apple Ads organisation identifier, the click date, the country or region of the ad, and whether it was a first download or a re-download. The campaign, ad group and keyword identifiers and the yes/no answer are set as analytics properties. The full record is also saved to your player record in our cloud database, linked to your Firebase user ID, so that purchase revenue can be matched to the ad that brought you. It contains no name, email address, device identifier or advertising identifier, and it is deleted with your player record when you delete your account. Firebase Crashlytics crash reporting is off until the consent check has run. In regions where privacy law requires consent (for example the EEA and UK), it is turned on only after you agree in the consent form, including to storing and accessing information on your device; elsewhere it is turned on by default. When on, it collects crash logs and stack traces, the state of the app when it crashed, error reports from the app (email addresses, account IDs and purchase transaction IDs are removed before they are sent; nothing is kept from before the consent check allows it), and device and OS information (device model, OS and app version) with a random installation ID. It is not linked to your account and is not used for tracking or advertising. If you withdraw consent in Settings → About → Manage Privacy Options, crash reporting stops and reports still stored on your device are deleted. Optional Pro Trading screens may request public market prices from providers such as Alpha Vantage, Finnhub, or Alpaca. Requests use HTTPS and may expose ordinary connection information such as IP address and user agent to the provider.
The Tycoon Card feature generates an image on your device. Money Tycoon does not upload the image. If you choose Share or Save, Android sends it to the destination you select.
The same feature uses the system share sheet. Money Tycoon does not upload the image; the destination you choose processes it under its own terms.

If you use Mogul Exchange chat, we process the messages you send (floor, direct messages and syndicates), reactions, your handle and display name, and any profile photo you upload. Photos are resized on your device before upload. This data is "Other User Content" and "Photos or Videos" in Apple's App Privacy terms, is linked to your account, and is used only to run the chat and to moderate it (automatic screening, reports and staff review). It is stored on our game server
, is visible to other players in the rooms you post in, and is deleted when you delete your account (Settings → Delete Account).

Before your first chat post we ask, once, for the year you were born. We store only the year, linked to your account on the same server, to decide how chat works for you; it is not shown to other players and cannot be changed afterwards. If the answer means you may be under 13, chat becomes read-only (the public Floor only, no direct messages, syndicates or profile photo), any profile photo is removed, and ads on that device are requested with Google's child-directed treatment and without the App Tracking Transparency prompt. The answer is kept if you start a new game and is deleted when you delete your account. This is "Other Data Types" in Apple's App Privacy terms.

EEA/UK users may withdraw consent and complain to their local supervisory authority. California residents may request to know, correct, or delete covered information and may opt out of sharing used for cross-context behavioural advertising. We do not discriminate for exercising privacy rights.

Money Tycoon is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from a child under 13. Chat asks for a birth year before a player's first post; a player whose answer means they may be under 13 can only read the public Floor, cannot post, send direct messages, join syndicates or upload a photo, and is served child-directed ads without the tracking prompt (see Chat, Messages and Profile Photos above). If you believe a child provided information, contact us so we can investigate and delete it.
